subject: science
passage: Mawsynram, a village in the Khasi Hills of northeastern India, is often listed among the wettest places on Earth. During the summer monsoon, moist winds blow north from the Bay of Bengal and meet the steep southern slopes of the hills. As the air is forced upward, it cools, and much of its moisture falls as rain on those slopes, where Mawsynram lies. By the time the air crosses the hills and descends on the northern side, it has lost much of its moisture. Places on the northern side of the hills therefore most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: receive more monsoon rain than Mawsynram, because the air there is cooler.
choices.B: receive considerably less monsoon rain than Mawsynram does.
choices.C: receive no rain at all during the summer monsoon season.
choices.D: receive their monsoon rain from winds blowing south rather than north.

explanation.why: The moist air drops much of its water on the southern slopes, where Mawsynram is. When the air reaches the northern side, it has "lost much of its moisture," so less rain can fall there.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The air reaching the northern side has already lost much of its moisture, so those places should get less rain, not more.
explanation.B: Correct. Air that has lost much of its moisture on the southern slopes has less left to drop on the northern side.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This goes too far: the air has lost much of its moisture, not all of it, so some rain is still possible.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes only winds blowing north and gives no information about winds from the north.
